_howto: THE ONE PLACE TO EDIT AT A RELEASE. Add a new object at the TOP of `releases` (version = semver, date = YYYY-MM-DD, title = a few words, sections = { New | Improved | Fixed | Removed: [items] }). The newest entry IS the app version: /api/health and the UI read it. `next` (optional) previews the upcoming release; its version must be greater than the newest release. 1.0.0 is reserved for an agreed 1.0: don't use it until that's decided. `npm run build` (and therefore every deploy) fails if this file is malformed or out of order (scripts/check-changelog.js).

New: Live results for West Virginia, Oregon, New Mexico, Nebraska, South Dakota, North Dakota, Alaska, Maryland, Indiana, Louisiana and Alabama from each state's official results site, with every contest those sites publish
West Virginia (Secretary of State): U.S. Senate, both U.S. House seats, Amendment 1, the legislature and judicial races, by county
Oregon, New Mexico, Nebraska and South Dakota: U.S. Senate, Governor, U.S. House, statewide offices and measures by county, plus every legislative, judicial and local contest
North Dakota: the same, as soon as its results site switches from the 2024 election to tonight's

Alaska (Division of Elections): U.S. Senate, U.S. House, Governor, the legislature, ballot measures and judicial retention, statewide with the vote-method split (first-choice counts in ranked-choice races)

Maryland (State Board of Elections): Governor, Comptroller, Attorney General, all 8 U.S. House seats, the General Assembly, judges, Questions 1–3 and every county contest, by county with early / election day / mail-in / provisional votes
Indiana (Election Division): all 9 U.S. House seats, Secretary of State, Comptroller and Treasurer by county, the General Assembly, judges and every county and local contest
Louisiana (Secretary of State): U.S. Senate, all 6 U.S. House seats, Public Service Commission, BESE, the 10 constitutional amendments and every parish and local race, by parish

Alabama (Secretary of State): Governor, Lieutenant Governor, U.S. Senate, the contested U.S. House seats and Attorney General, by county (the first page of the state's results; the rest of the ballot isn't available to us)
Hawaii (Office of Elections): source ready but switched off until its first results file tonight has been checked

Fixed: Florida's "Official results" link goes to Florida Election Watch, the Secretary of State's election-night results site

releases.title: Polish: tooltips, candidate faces, measure positions

New: Every candidate row has a small circle with their initials, tinted by party. Official or openly licensed photos will appear once each is checked by hand, and only in contests where every major candidate has one, so no candidate gets a face while an opponent gets initials. Each photo shows its credit and license

Ballot measures always list both major parties: Support, Oppose or Neutral once a position is checked against the party's own source, "Not yet verified" while it is being checked, or "No published position"
Campaign websites for both sides of a measure, as listed in the official voter guide or filings (including measures the Legislature referred)

States without live results now say why: the results site doesn't allow automated access, the state doesn't publish live statewide results we can read, or we haven't connected it yet, always next to the official results link
Improved: Map tooltips are wider (320–420 px) so candidate names wrap instead of being cut off, and vote counts never break mid-number
On phones, tapping a state or county shows its details in a panel at the bottom of the screen; tap again (or the button) to open it
Checked party positions and campaign websites for California, Colorado, Florida, Idaho, North Carolina, Ohio and Virginia measures are now shown
Map legend: "No live results here" (same hatching)
Fixed: Florida write-in candidates (listed as "WRI") are shown on the write-in line, not as party candidates
When a results site has a temporary server error, we keep checking every minute (then at most every 2 minutes) instead of backing off for up to 10 minutes

New: Florida results, from the Division of Elections' Florida Election Watch files (Senate, Governor, U.S. House, Amendments 1-3 and every other contest in the state file), with county maps
Fixed: Governor tickets show the candidate for Governor, with the running mate stored alongside, never in their place
Texas "last updated" time is read as UTC; it was shown six hours in the future, which also moved the national Last update
Ohio no longer shows "0 ballots cast" while votes are being counted; the number is shown once the source publishes it

New: Top race view, now the default: each state colored by its top race on the ballot (U.S. Senate, else Governor, else the U.S. House popular vote), with its other major races listed in the tooltip
Federal / State selector: U.S. Senate and U.S. House, or Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State and every other statewide office our sources carry
"All races" tab for each state: every contest in its official feed (state legislature, county, local, judicial, ballot questions), grouped and searchable, with each contest's candidates
Ballot measure details from official sources: ballot title, official summary, who placed it on the ballot, registered opposition, the legislature's vote to refer and the full ballot text
Official results link for every state, and the source and its last update for every number
Improved: Candidates by name everywhere: tooltips, the state totals, county details and every contest list show each candidate with a party tag, votes and %, never lumped into "Other" (the U.S. House view stays a statewide sum by party)
Contests that elect several people (vote for 2 or more) show their top candidates instead of a misleading two-way margin

Fixed: Live updates now always show the new numbers instead of a copy cached for up to 45 seconds, and numbers can no longer step backwards
The page catches up after a lost connection, a server restart or a sleeping tab, and checks for new numbers every minute if nothing has arrived
New: "Updated Xs ago" next to Last update, a visible "Reconnecting…" when the live connection drops, and a "New version available" banner after a deploy

Fixed: Vermont % reporting now counts every town; it showed nearly 100% when only a handful of towns had reported

New: The new dark design: national map shaded by margin, state drill-down with a county map for every state whose source has counties, and a details panel
Details for each state and county: turnout so far, precincts reporting, ballots left to count (where published) and the vote split by method (mail/early, election day, provisional)
Ballot measures sidebar with the source's own titles; "too early" until enough is reported, then which side leads
This changelog, inside the app
New official sources: Georgia, Virginia, Utah, Washington, Rhode Island, Idaho, Texas, North Carolina, Ohio, California, Arkansas, Connecticut, Vermont and Delaware
Improved: Every source now records registered voters, ballots cast, precincts and its own "last updated" time when it publishes them
Faster under heavy traffic: responses are cached briefly and shared through Cloudflare
Live updates fall back to polling if WebSockets are blocked

New: A national map you can switch between races
A state view, broken down by county where the state's results source publishes counties
A sidebar for ballot measures
Results update live over Socket.io: no page refresh needed
A Clarity ENR adapter that reads results for Colorado and Iowa
